improvements.title: Improved Articles
improvements.subtitle: Below you can find articles which need to be improved to start ranking better on Google and AI search.
improvements.explainer: We continuously review how the articles on your website perform in Google Search. When the data shows a clear opportunity to rank better, we rewrite that article, changing only the parts that need it.

scan.title: Scan performance
scan.description: Through Google Search Console, we track clicks, impressions, click-through rate and rankings for every article on your website.

rewrite.title: Rewrite with purpose
rewrite.description: On each improvement day, we rewrite the article with the clearest opportunity. We prepare it the day before, so it's ready for review on the day itself.

review.title: You stay in control
review.description: Approve or reject each change one by one. Nothing goes live until you approve, unless auto-approve is on. Safety-flagged rewrites always wait for your review.

howItWorks.eligibility: Articles that already perform well are left alone. To qualify, a page needs at least 90 days in Google Search and real search demand. Pages improved in the last 6 months, or rejected in the last 4 weeks, are skipped. When several pages qualify, the one with the most impressions goes first.

measure.title: Measure the impact
measure.description: About two weeks after an improvement goes live, we compare its clicks and impressions with the period before, so you can see what changed.

howItWorks.changesScope: We only change what the opportunity calls for. An article with a weak click-through rate gets a new title and description, while an outdated one gets its facts refreshed without new sections being added.

problemDetails.robots_txt_missing: We couldn't find /robots.txt. This small file tells search engines which pages they may read.
problemDetails.robots_txt_incorrect: Your robots.txt stops Google or Bing from reading your homepage, so it can't show in results.
problemDetails.sitemap_missing: We couldn't find a sitemap. It lists your pages so search engines find new ones quickly.
problemDetails.sitemap_incorrect: Your sitemap isn't valid XML, often because of a blank first line or a hidden character, so search engines may skip it.
problemDetails.llm_txt_missing: There is no /llms.txt. This file gives AI assistants a short guide to your most important pages.
problemDetails.ssl_missing: Your site doesn't load securely. Browsers warn visitors and search engines rank it lower.
problemDetails.meta_title_missing: The page has no title. Google shows the title as the clickable link in results.
problemDetails.meta_title_length: Aim for 45–60 characters. Longer titles get cut off in Google and shorter ones say too little.
problemDetails.meta_title_duplicates: The page has two or more title tags, so search engines may pick the wrong one.
problemDetails.meta_title_uniqueness: Several pages share this title, so search engines can't tell them apart.
problemDetails.meta_title_irrelevant: The title doesn't describe what's on the page, which costs clicks and rankings.
problemDetails.meta_description_missing: Without one, Google picks random text from the page to show under your link.
problemDetails.meta_description_length: Aim for 150–160 characters so the whole text shows under your link in Google.
problemDetails.meta_description_duplicates: The page has two or more description tags, so search engines may show the wrong one.
problemDetails.meta_description_uniqueness: Several pages share this description, so they look the same in search results.
problemDetails.meta_description_irrelevant: The description doesn't sum up the page, so fewer people click.
problemDetails.h1_missing: Each page needs one H1 that says what it's about. It helps search engines and screen readers.
problemDetails.h1_multiple: Use exactly one H1 per page so the main topic is clear.
problemDetails.canonical_missing: A canonical tag tells search engines which address is the main one, so copies don't compete.
problemDetails.canonical_duplicates: Two or more canonical tags confuse search engines. Keep one.
problemDetails.canonical_incorrect: The page says its main version lives on a different domain, so this page may not rank.
problemDetails.broken_link: A link on the page leads to an error, so visitors and crawlers hit a dead end.
problemDetails.page_speed_low: Google PageSpeed scores the page below 80 on desktop. Slow pages lose visitors and rankings.
problemDetails.image_large: Images over 100 KB slow the page down. Compress them or save them as WebP.
problemDetails.image_missing_alt_text: Alt text describes an image for screen readers and search engines.
problemDetails.image_poor_alt_text: The alt text is a file name, a generic word, or too short or long to describe the image.
problemDetails.image_broken: An image doesn't load, so visitors see an empty space.
problemDetails.image_unknown_format: We couldn't tell what kind of image this is, so some browsers may not show it.
problemDetails.json_ld_missing: Structured data (JSON-LD) tells Google and AI assistants what the page is, like a product, an article or a business.
problemDetails.json_ld_incorrect: The page has structured data, but it's incomplete or doesn't match the page.
problemDetails.missing_content_gaps: People ask questions about your topic that this page doesn't answer. AI assistants quote pages that do.

robots_txt_missing.title: Missing robots.txt file
robots_txt_missing.description: robots.txt is the first file crawlers look for. Without it, Google and AI crawlers can't find your sitemap through it, and you have no way to tell them what to skip.
robots_txt_missing.action: Add a robots.txt file at yoursite.com/robots.txt that allows crawling and includes a Sitemap line with your sitemap URL.

robots_txt_incorrect.title: Incorrect robots.txt configuration
robots_txt_incorrect.description: Your robots.txt blocks search engine crawlers such as Googlebot or Bingbot from your homepage, so your site can drop out of Google, Bing and the AI answers built on them.
robots_txt_incorrect.action: Remove the rule that blocks the crawlers listed in this issue, for example Disallow: / under User-agent: *.

sitemap_missing.title: Missing sitemap
sitemap_missing.description: A sitemap lists the pages you want found. Without one, Google and AI crawlers rely on links alone and can miss new or deeper pages.
sitemap_missing.action: Publish an XML sitemap at yoursite.com/sitemap.xml that lists your important pages, add it to robots.txt and submit it in Google Search Console.

sitemap_incorrect.title: Incorrect sitemap XML
sitemap_incorrect.description: Your sitemap has blank lines, hidden characters or broken XML, so search engines may not be able to read it at all.
sitemap_incorrect.action: Remove blank lines and hidden characters so the XML declaration is on the very first line, then check the file with a sitemap validator.

llm_txt_missing.title: Missing llms.txt file
llm_txt_missing.description: llms.txt is an emerging standard: a short, plain-text guide to your business and key pages, written for AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude. We couldn't find a valid one on your site.
llm_txt_missing.action: Add a plain-text llms.txt file at yoursite.com/llms.txt with a one-paragraph summary of your business and links to your most important pages.

json_ld_missing.title: Missing JSON-LD schema
json_ld_missing.description: Structured data (JSON-LD) tells search engines exactly what a page is, such as an article, a product or a business, and helps AI assistants understand it. Without it, the page can't get rich results such as review stars or prices.
json_ld_missing.action: Add JSON-LD that fits the page, for example Article for blog posts, Product for product pages, or Organization or LocalBusiness for your homepage.

json_ld_incorrect.title: Incorrect JSON-LD schema
json_ld_incorrect.description: This page has structured data, but it leaves out details that describe the page, so Google and AI assistants get an incomplete picture.
json_ld_incorrect.action: Update the JSON-LD with the suggested schema in this issue, then check it with Google's Rich Results Test.

meta_title_length.title: Meta title length issue
meta_title_length.description: Google cuts off titles longer than about 60 characters, and very short titles say too little. The title is what people read before deciding to click.
meta_title_length.action: Rewrite the title to 45–60 characters, with the most important words first.

meta_title_duplicates.title: Duplicate meta title tags
meta_title_duplicates.description: This page has more than one title tag, so search engines have to guess which one to show.
meta_title_duplicates.action: Remove the extra title tags so the page has one. Duplicates usually come from a theme and an SEO plugin both adding a title.

meta_title_uniqueness.title: Title duplicated across multiple pages
meta_title_uniqueness.description: When several pages share a title, Google can't tell them apart and they end up competing for the same searches.
meta_title_uniqueness.action: Give each page its own title that says what makes that page different.

meta_title_missing.title: Missing meta title
meta_title_missing.description: Without a title, Google makes one up from the page content, and it's usually less clear and less clickable than one you'd write.
meta_title_missing.action: Add a title of 45–60 characters that says what the page is about, with the most important words first.

meta_title_irrelevant.title: Irrelevant meta title
meta_title_irrelevant.description: The title doesn't match what the page is about, so Google may replace it in results and visitors who click don't find what they expected.
meta_title_irrelevant.action: Rewrite the title to describe what the page actually covers, using the words people search for.

meta_description_length.title: Meta description length
meta_description_length.description: Google cuts off descriptions longer than about 160 characters, and very short ones don't give people a reason to click.
meta_description_length.action: Rewrite the description to 110–160 characters, with the key point first.

meta_description_missing.title: Missing meta description
meta_description_missing.description: Without a meta description, Google picks a snippet from the page itself, which is often less convincing than a summary you write.
meta_description_missing.action: Add a meta description of 110–160 characters that summarizes the page and gives people a reason to click.

meta_description_duplicates.title: Duplicate meta description tags
meta_description_duplicates.description: This page has more than one meta description tag, so search engines have to guess which one to show.
meta_description_duplicates.action: Remove the extra meta description tags so the page has one. Duplicates usually come from a theme and an SEO plugin both adding one.

meta_description_uniqueness.title: Not unique meta description
meta_description_uniqueness.description: When several pages share a description, they look the same in search results and people can't tell which one to click.
meta_description_uniqueness.action: Write a description for each page that sums up what that specific page offers.

meta_description_irrelevant.title: Irrelevant meta description
meta_description_irrelevant.description: The description doesn't match what the page is about, so Google often replaces it with its own snippet and visitors may not find what they expected.
meta_description_irrelevant.action: Rewrite the description to summarize what the page actually covers, using the words people search for.

page_speed_low.title: Low page speed
page_speed_low.description: This page scores below 80 in Google PageSpeed Insights. Slow pages lose visitors, especially on mobile, and page experience is one of the signals Google uses to rank pages.
page_speed_low.action: Work through the suggestions in the PageSpeed report, usually compressing images, removing unused scripts and turning on caching. Aim for 80 or higher.

h1_missing.title: Missing H1 tag
h1_missing.description: The H1 is the main heading of a page. Without one, readers, screen readers and AI assistants lose a clear signal of what the page is about.
h1_missing.action: Add one H1 at the top of the page that states its main topic.

h1_multiple.title: Multiple H1 tags
h1_multiple.description: With more than one H1 there's no single main heading, so it's less clear to readers, screen readers and AI assistants what the page is mainly about.
h1_multiple.action: Keep one H1 for the main topic and change the others to H2 or H3 subheadings.

canonical_missing.title: Missing canonical URL
canonical_missing.description: A canonical tag tells search engines which URL is the main version of a page. Without it, Google chooses one itself and may pick a copy, such as a URL with tracking parameters.
canonical_missing.action: Add a canonical tag that points to this page's own URL.

canonical_duplicates.title: Multiple canonical URLs
canonical_duplicates.description: This page has more than one canonical tag, so search engines can't tell which URL is the main one and may ignore them all.
canonical_duplicates.action: Remove the extra canonical tags so one remains. Duplicates usually come from a theme and an SEO plugin both adding one.

canonical_incorrect.title: Incorrect canonical URL
canonical_incorrect.description: The canonical tag points to another website, which tells search engines to show that site's page instead of yours.
canonical_incorrect.action: Change the canonical tag to a URL on your own domain, usually this page's own URL.

image_large.title: Large image
image_large.description: Images over 150 KB are often the main reason pages load slowly, especially on mobile, and slow pages lose visitors.
image_large.action: Resize the image to the size it's shown at and compress it below 150 KB. Saving it as WebP usually makes it much smaller.

image_poor_alt_text.title: Poor image alt text
image_poor_alt_text.description: This image's alt text doesn't describe what it shows, so screen reader users, search engines and AI assistants can't tell what's in it.
image_poor_alt_text.action: Rewrite the alt text as a short, specific description of what the image shows.

too_short.title: Image alt text too short
too_short.description: The image has alt text, but it is under 5 characters — too short to describe the image for accessibility and image SEO.
too_short.action: Expand the alt text into a short description of the image (at least 5 characters)

too_long.title: Image alt text too long
too_long.description: The alt text is over 160 characters. Screen reader users have to listen to all of it, and longer details belong in a caption or the page text.
too_long.action: Shorten the alt text to 160 characters or fewer while keeping it descriptive

generic.title: Generic image alt text
generic.description: The image's alt text is a generic word like "image" or "logo" that does not describe what the image shows.
generic.action: Replace the generic alt text with a short description of what the image shows

filename.title: Image alt text is a filename
filename.description: The alt text is a file name, so it tells screen readers, search engines and AI assistants nothing about what the image shows.
filename.action: Replace the filename with a short description of what the image shows

image_missing_alt_text.title: Missing alt text
image_missing_alt_text.description: Alt text tells screen readers, search engines and AI assistants what an image shows. Without it, screen reader users miss the image and it's less likely to appear in image search.
image_missing_alt_text.action: Add alt text that describes what the image shows in a short phrase.

image_broken.title: Broken image
image_broken.description: This image doesn't load, so visitors see a broken placeholder and the image can't appear in image search.
image_broken.action: Fix the image URL or upload the image again, or remove it if you no longer need it.

image_unknown_format.title: Unknown image format
image_unknown_format.description: We couldn't tell what type of image this is, which usually means the server sends it with the wrong file type, so some browsers may not show it.
image_unknown_format.action: Save the image as JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF or SVG and make sure your server sends the matching file type.

ssl_missing.title: Missing SSL certificate
ssl_missing.description: Your site has no working SSL certificate (it's missing, expired or invalid), so browsers warn visitors that it's not secure, and Google prefers secure sites in its rankings.
ssl_missing.action: Install or renew the SSL certificate (most hosts include a free one) and redirect every HTTP address to HTTPS.

broken_link.title: Broken link
broken_link.description: This link leads to a page that doesn't work, so visitors who click it hit a dead end.
broken_link.action: Update the link to the right URL, point it to a working page on the same topic, or remove it.

missing_content_gaps.title: Missing content gaps
missing_content_gaps.description: This page doesn't cover topics your potential customers search for in Google and ask AI assistants about, so you miss those visitors.
missing_content_gaps.action: Add sections that answer the missing topics and questions listed for this page, or create new pages for them.

feed.title: Generate your RSS feed URL
feed.description: Duda pulls your articles from an <bold>RSS feed</bold>. Generate the URL below, then add it to your Duda site — that's the whole setup.
feed.copyNote: <bold>Copy this URL</bold> — you'll paste it into Duda in the next step.
feed.hint: Tip: change <bold>limit=10</bold> in the URL to control <bold>how many articles</bold> Duda shows.
feed.generateHint: Generate your RSS feed URL. It's unique to your site and already includes everything Duda needs — there's no separate key to manage.
feed.regenerateNote: Regenerating creates a new URL and disables the old one — if you've already added it to Duda, update it there with the new URL.

addFeed.title: Add the RSS feed to Duda
addFeed.description: Add Duda's built-in <bold>RSS Feed</bold> widget to the page where you want your articles, then paste your feed URL.
addFeed.intro: Do this in the Duda editor. Open your site from your Duda dashboard:
addFeed.step1: Open your site in the <bold>Duda Website Editor</bold>.
addFeed.step2: In the left sidebar, click <bold>Add → Elements</bold>, search <bold>“RSS Feed”</bold>, and <bold>drag</bold> the widget onto the page where you want your articles.
addFeed.step3: The <bold>RSS Feed Content</bold> panel usually opens automatically when you drop the widget. If it doesn't, right-click the widget and select <bold>Edit Content</bold> (in Flex mode and Editor 2.0, use the widget's floating <bold>Edit Content</bold> button).
addFeed.step4: <bold>Paste the RSS feed URL</bold> you copied into the field, adjust the display settings (number of posts, layout), then click <bold>Publish</bold>.
addFeed.displayNote: The RSS Feed widget <bold>displays</bold> your articles on this page, it doesn't add them to Duda's native Blog. Want real blog posts instead? The next step imports the same feed into your Duda Blog.
addFeed.helpLink: Stuck? See Duda's RSS Feed widget guide
addFeed.mediaAlt: Adding and configuring the RSS Feed widget in the Duda editor

blogImport.title: Import your articles into Duda's Blog
blogImport.description: Duda's native <bold>Blog</bold> can import the same feed, turning your articles into real blog posts on your site.
blogImport.intro: Do this in the Duda editor, on the site where you want the posts:
blogImport.step1: Open your site in the <bold>Duda Website Editor</bold>.
blogImport.step2: In the left sidebar, click <bold>Blog</bold>, then open the <bold>Import</bold> tab.
blogImport.step3: <bold>Paste the RSS feed URL</bold> you copied into the <bold>Enter RSS feed URL</bold> field.
blogImport.step4: Click <bold>Import Posts</bold>, then <bold>Publish</bold> your site so the posts go live.
blogImport.mediaAlt: Importing an RSS feed from the Blog panel in the Duda editor

connected.title: You're all set

connected.verify1: Publish your Duda site if you haven't already
connected.verify2: Open your live site and go to the page with the RSS Feed widget, or to your Blog if you imported the posts
connected.verify3: Confirm your BabyLoveGrowth articles appear (it can take Duda a few minutes to pull the feed the first time)
connected.note: Duda syncs from the RSS feed, so make sure <bold>at least one article is published</bold> for it to show content.

step1.howToAddBlog: How to add a blog in Wix
step1.checkBlog: The <bold>Wix Blog</bold> app is added to my site

step2.title: Find your Site ID
step2.description: Open your Wix dashboard and look at the URL in your <bold>browser address bar.</bold>
step2.mediaAlt: Finding the Site ID in the Wix dashboard URL

step3.title: Create your API key
step3.description: Generate the key and set its permissions — everything happens on one Wix screen.
step3.intro: The button below takes you straight to your Wix API Keys page. You may be asked to sign in.
step3.step3: Under <bold>Permissions</bold>, expand <bold>All site permissions</bold> and turn on both of these:
step3.siteAccessNote: If Wix asks which sites the key can access, pick <bold>All sites</bold> — or make sure your site is included. A key limited to other sites is rejected with a 403 error.
step3.mediaAlt: Generating an API key in Wix Account Settings

step4.title: Verify your email & copy the key
step4.description: To finish creating the key, Wix asks you to <bold>verify your identity</bold>.
step4.step1: Click <bold>Generate Key</bold> — Wix sends a verification code to your email
step4.step2: Enter the code and click <bold>Verify & Generate Key</bold>
step4.step3: <bold>Copy the key</bold> that appears — you'll paste it in the next step
step4.keyFormatHint: Wix keys are long, span <bold>several lines</bold>, and start with <bold>IST.</bold> — that's normal. Copy the whole thing.
step4.important: <bold>Important:</bold> <subtle>Wix only shows this key</subtle> <bold>once</bold>. <subtle>Copy it before leaving the page.</subtle>

step5.title: Paste your key & connect
step5.description: Paste the API key and choose how articles should be posted. We verify the key with Wix before saving.

step5.noBlogTitle: Your Wix site doesn't have a blog yet
step5.noBlogBody: Your key and Site ID are fine — but the site has no <bold>Wix Blog</bold> app, so there's nothing to publish into. Add it (it's free), then click Connect again.
step5.permissionHintTitle: Wix rejected the key. The three most common causes:
step5.permissionHint1: 1. The key is missing the <bold>Wix Blog</bold> permission — check its permission list.
step5.permissionHint2: 2. The key was created by a <bold>co-owner or collaborator</bold> — it must come from the site owner's account.
step5.permissionHint3: 3. The key's <bold>site access</bold> is limited to specific sites that don't include this one.

connected.description: Your site is linked. Verify it's working by publishing a test article.
connected.label: Wix site
connected.step3: In Wix, go to your site dashboard → Blog
connected.step4: You'll see the article appear there.

step1.title: Before you start
step1.description: Just one quick check — it prevents almost every problem later on.
step1.prereqAdmin: I can sign in to Shopify as the <bold>store owner</bold> (or my account is allowed to create apps)
step1.prereqAdminHelp: Not sure? Here's how Shopify permissions work
step1.timeEstimate: The setup takes about 10 minutes and we'll guide you through every click. Your store, theme and products are never touched — this connection can only read and publish blog posts.

step2.title: Find your store name
step2.description: Every Shopify store has its own .myshopify.com address. Paste it below — we check it with Shopify as you type.
step2.domainsHint: The button opens your Shopify domain settings, where your .myshopify.com address is listed.
step2.copyHelp: Paste the whole address if you like (e.g. <pill>na70yq-bn.myshopify.com</pill> ) — we'll trim it for you.
step2.label: Store name
step2.storeNotFound: We couldn't find this store. Double-check the spelling, or copy the address from your Shopify domain settings and paste it here.
step2.mediaAlt: Finding your .myshopify.com address in the Shopify domain settings

step3.title: Create an app in the Shopify Dev Dashboard
step3.description: The connection works through a small private app that you create once. No coding involved — just a few clicks.
step3.signInHint: If Shopify asks you to sign in, use the same account you use for your store.
step3.item1: Click <bold>Create app</bold> in the top-right corner.
step3.item3: Give the app any name you like and click <bold>Create</bold> — or copy ours:
step3.mediaAlt: Creating an app in the Shopify Dev Dashboard

step4.title: Give the app blog permissions
step4.description: Your new app needs permission to read and write blog posts — nothing else.
step4.item1: After creating the app, you land on its configuration form. (If you don't see it, open <bold>Versions</bold> and start a new version.)
step4.item2: Under <bold>API access</bold>, click <bold>Select scopes</bold>, search for "content" and tick both:
step4.hint: Everything else can stay exactly as it is — including the pre-filled <bold>App URL</bold>. This app has no visible pages, so the URL is never shown to anyone.
step4.appUrlFallback: Only if the App URL box is empty, paste:
step4.mediaAlt: Selecting the read_content and write_content scopes

step5.title: Release the version
step5.description: A release saves your app's configuration and makes it installable.
step5.item2: The version name can stay empty — just click <bold>Release</bold> again.
step5.reassurance: Nothing changes on your live store yet. A release only prepares the app so it can be installed in the next step.

step6.title: Install the app on your store
step6.description: Now connect the app to your store so it's allowed to publish.
step6.backInDashboard: This step happens back in the Shopify Dev Dashboard (not in your store admin):
step6.item1: In the <bold>Apps</bold> list, click the app you just created (e.g. <bold>BabyLoveGrowth Blog Publisher</bold>).
step6.item2: You land on the app's <bold>Overview</bold> page. In the <bold>Installs</bold> card (top right), click <bold>Install app</bold>.
step6.item3: Select <bold>{store}</bold> from the list and confirm the installation.
step6.troubleshootTitle: Don't see your store in the list?
step6.troubleshootBody: The app and the store must belong to the same Shopify organization, and your account needs permission to install apps. If you're a collaborator, or the store is owned by a different account, ask the store owner to create the app and complete these steps from their account.
step6.reviewNoticeBody: That's expected. Shopify shows this notice for any app you create yourself instead of installing from the Shopify App Store — it only means Shopify hasn't reviewed it, not that anything is wrong. This is your own private app, with permission limited to reading and publishing blog content. It's safe to click Install, and publishing works exactly as expected.
step6.mediaAlt: Installing the app on a Shopify store

step7.title: Open your app's Settings
step7.description: Your Client ID and Client secret live on the app's Settings page in the Dev Dashboard — you'll copy them in the next step.
step7.notStoreSettings: After installing, Shopify left you in your store admin — but this step happens back in the Dev Dashboard. It's a different Settings page than your store's.
step7.item1: Open your app and click <bold>Settings</bold> in its left sidebar (bottom left, below Monitoring, Logs and Versions).
step7.item2: Find the <bold>Client credentials</bold> section with the <bold>Client ID</bold> and <bold>Client secret</bold> fields, and keep this tab open.
step7.mediaAlt: The app Settings page with Client ID and Client secret

step8.title: Paste your credentials
step8.description: Copy both values from the Settings tab you just opened. We verify them with Shopify automatically — you'll see a green check when everything works.
step8.verified: Connected! We found {count} blog(s) in your store.
step8.errInvalidClient: Shopify doesn't recognize these credentials. Make sure you copied the full Client ID and Client secret from your app's Settings page (no extra spaces).
step8.errAppNotInstalled: Your credentials are correct, but the app isn't installed on this store yet. Go back to the Install step, finish the installation, then re-check.
step8.errShopNotPermitted: This store ({store}) isn't in the same Shopify organization as your app. Create the app while signed in to the account that owns the store, or ask the store owner to do it.
step8.errNoBlogs: Your credentials work, but there's no blog in your store yet. Add one in Shopify under Online Store → Blog posts → Manage blogs, then re-check.
step8.errGeneric: We couldn't verify these credentials. Double-check the values and that the app is installed on your store.
step8.stuckTitle: Still stuck? Our team can help you right away.

step9.title: Choose where and how to publish
step9.description: Last details — pick the blog we should publish to and how new articles should appear.
step9.noBlogs: No blogs found in your Shopify store
step9.publishImmediatelyDesc: Articles go live on your Shopify blog as soon as they're published here.
step9.draftDesc: Articles arrive as drafts in Shopify, so you review and publish them yourself.
